audit.summary: Four promise problems are formalized as pairs of yes/no bit-string languages over explicit binary encodings of instances. Each is proved NP-hard in the Karp sense: every NP language, defined via a polynomial-time TM2 verifier with polynomially bounded certificates, poly-time many-one reduces to the promise problem. The problems are Euclidean GapCVP with gap n^{1/400} and integer targets, binary nearest codeword and binary syndrome decoding with gap n^{1/200}, and ℓ_p GapCVP with gap n^{1/(200p)} for every rational p ≥ 1. The definitions track the paper closely. The main caveats: the ℓ_p statement (gap exponent, p ranging only over rationals, rational targets allowed) cannot be checked against the excerpt, and the syndrome-decoding NO set additionally requires the system Hx=b to be consistent, which is a stronger (fine) choice.

glossary.plain: L ⊆ {0,1}* is in NP iff there are a polynomial bound q and a poly-time (TM2) verifier V such that x ∈ L ⇔ ∃ certificate c with |c| ≤ q(|x|) and V(x,c)=1.
A poly-time map f on bit strings such that x ∈ L ⇒ f(x) ∈ YES and x ∉ L ⇒ f(x) ∈ NO.
glossary.standard_concept: Karp reduction to a promise problem

glossary.plain: Every NP language Karp-reduces to the promise problem.
glossary.standard_concept: NP-hardness of a promise problem under deterministic poly-time many-one reductions

glossary.plain: YES: encodings of (n>0, nonsingular B∈Z^{n×n}, t∈Z^n, r∈Q>0) with dist_2(t,L(B)) ≤ r. NO: same shape with dist_2(t,L(B)) > n^{1/400} r. The lattice is generated by the columns of B.
glossary.note: Distances are compared via squares, which is equivalent because both sides are nonnegative.

glossary.plain: YES: (G∈F2^{n×k}, u, R>0, n>0) with ∃c, wt(u−Gc) ≤ R. NO: ∀c, wt(u−Gc) > n^{1/200} R.
glossary.note: The code is the column span of G rather than the row span; this is only a notational convention.

glossary.plain: YES: (H, b, R>0, n>0) with ∃x, Hx=b and wt(x) ≤ R. NO: Hx=b is consistent and every solution has wt(x) > n^{1/200} R.
glossary.note: The NO set requires consistency of Hx=b, so it is smaller than a definition that treats inconsistent systems as NO. This makes Lean stronger.

glossary.plain: For rational p ≥ 1. YES: well-formed (B, t∈Q^n, r) with min_v ‖t−Bv‖_p ≤ r. NO: ‖t−Bv‖_p > n^{1/(200p)} r for all v.
glossary.note: The paper's exact ℓ_p statement is not in the excerpt. Targets are not required to be integral here, unlike the ℓ_2 version.

lean_claims.plain: Every NP language Karp-reduces to the promise problem (YES: dist_2(t,L(B)) ≤ r; NO: dist_2 > n^{1/400} r), with B nonsingular integer, t integer, r>0 rational, n>0.
Every NP language Karp-reduces to binary nearest codeword with gap n^{1/200}, where n is the block length, R ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1.
Every NP language Karp-reduces to binary syndrome decoding with gap n^{1/200}. NO instances must have a consistent syndrome system.
For every rational p ≥ 1, every NP language Karp-reduces to ℓ_p GapCVP with gap n^{1/(200p)}, using a nonsingular integer basis, rational target and positive rational radius.

paper_claims.plain: There is a deterministic poly-time map from 3SAT formulas to (B nonsingular in Z^{n×n}, t∈Z^n, r∈Q>0). Satisfiable ⇒ dist_2 ≤ r; unsatisfiable ⇒ dist_2 > n^{1/400} r. Hence GapCVP_{n^{1/400}} is NP-hard.
Binary nearest codeword and binary syndrome decoding are NP-hard to approximate within n^{1/200}, with n the block length, under deterministic poly-time many-one reductions.
Not in excerpt (fixed-finite-norm GapCVP hardness mentioned only).

coverage.why: Same instance shape and gap. NP-hardness is stated for all NP languages rather than via 3SAT, which is equivalent by Cook–Levin.
Matches. Lean additionally requires R>0 and n>0, which is slightly stronger.
The NO set additionally requires a consistent system.
The exact paper statement is not in the excerpt. Lean covers only rational p and allows rational targets.

flags.explanation: The gap exponent 1/(200p) and the parameter range cannot be checked against the excerpt. Here p ranges only over rationals ≥ 1, whereas the paper likely says any fixed real p ∈ [1,∞).

Unlike gapCVP400, no hasIntegerTarget requirement is imposed, so targets may be rational. This enlarges the YES/NO sets, which is a mildly weaker hardness claim than an integer-target version. Scaling B and t by a common denominator makes the two essentially equivalent.
The NO set requires Hx=b to be consistent, so the reduction must output consistent systems on unsatisfiable inputs. This is stronger than a definition treating inconsistent systems as NO.
The disjointness fields are sorry'd inside the target definitions. They are proof fields and do not affect the statement. Disjointness is in fact true, since n ≥ 1 and r > 0 give n^{1/400} r ≥ r.

result.claim: The YES and NO promise predicates of GapCVP400 (gapYES400 and gapNO400) cannot hold simultaneously on an instance. This is the instance-level core of the sorry'd `disjoint` field of gapCVP400Promise, and it holds because the gap factor n^(1/400) is at least 1 and the radius is positive.

namespace GapCVP.Comparator
open scoped BigOperators
theorem probe_restate_2  :
    (IsNPHardPromise gapCVP400Promise) ↔
    (∀ language : BitLanguage, IsNP language = true → ∃ map : List Bool → List Bool, Nonempty (GapCVP.BitTM map) ∧ (∀ input : List Bool, language input = true → yesLanguage input = true) ∧ (∀ input : List Bool, ¬ (language input = true) → noLanguage input = true)) := by
  unfold IsNPHardPromise
  simp only [decide_eq_true_eq]
  constructor
  · intro h language hl
    obtain ⟨r⟩ := h language hl
    exact ⟨r.map, r.polynomial_time, r.completeness, r.soundness⟩
  · intro h language hl
    obtain ⟨m, hm, hc, hs⟩ := h language hl
    exact ⟨⟨m, hm, hc, hs⟩⟩
end GapCVP.Comparator

namespace GapCVP.Comparator
open scoped BigOperators
theorem probe_restate_12  :
    (IsNPHardPromise binaryNearestCodewordPromise) ↔
    (∀ language : BitLanguage, IsNP language = true → ∃ map : List Bool → List Bool, Nonempty (GapCVP.BitTM map) ∧ (∀ input : List Bool, language input = true → ∃ record : BinaryNearestCodewordInstance, encodeBinaryNearestCodewordInstance record = map input ∧ 0 < record.blockLength ∧ 0 < record.radius ∧ ∃ coefficients : Fin record.generatorRank → ZMod 2, hammingNorm (binaryNearestTarget record - binaryNearestCodeword record coefficients) ≤ record.radius) ∧ (∀ input : List Bool, ¬ language input = true → ∃ record : BinaryNearestCodewordInstance, encodeBinaryNearestCodewordInstance record = map input ∧ 0 < record.blockLength ∧ 0 < record.radius ∧ ∀ coefficients : Fin record.generatorRank → ZMod 2, binaryCodeGapFactor record.blockLength * (record.radius : ℝ) < (hammingNorm (binaryNearestTarget record - binaryNearestCodeword record coefficients) : ℝ))) := by
  simp only [IsNPHardPromise, binaryNearestCodewordPromise, decide_eq_true_eq]
  constructor
  · intro h language hl
    obtain ⟨r⟩ := h language hl
    refine ⟨r.map, r.polynomial_time, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro input hin
      have := r.completeness input hin
      simpa only [binaryNearestCodewordPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using this
    · intro input hin
      have := r.soundness input hin
      simpa only [binaryNearestCodewordPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using this
  · intro h language hl
    obtain ⟨map, hmap, hc, hs⟩ := h language hl
    refine ⟨{ map := map, polynomial_time := hmap, completeness := ?_, soundness := ?_ }⟩
    · intro input hin
      simpa only [binaryNearestCodewordPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using hc input hin
    · intro input hin
      simpa only [binaryNearestCodewordPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using hs input hin
end GapCVP.Comparator

restatements.english: Every language in NP has a polynomial-time computable map on bit strings that sends each input to the encoding of a binary syndrome-decoding instance. If the input is in the language, the instance is a YES instance: some word of Hamming weight at most the radius has syndrome equal to the target. If the input is not in the language, the instance is a NO instance: it is consistent (some word has the target syndrome), and every word with that syndrome has Hamming weight greater than n^(1/200) times the radius, where n is the block length.

namespace GapCVP.Comparator
open scoped BigOperators
theorem probe_restate_22  :
    (IsNPHardPromise binarySyndromeDecodingPromise) ↔
    (∀ language : BitLanguage, IsNP language = true → ∃ map : List Bool → List Bool, Nonempty (BitTM map) ∧ (∀ input : List Bool, language input = true → ∃ record : BinarySyndromeDecodingInstance, encodeBinarySyndromeDecodingInstance record = map input ∧ 0 < record.blockLength ∧ 0 < record.radius ∧ ∃ word : Fin record.blockLength → ZMod 2, binarySyndromeProduct record word = binarySyndromeTarget record ∧ hammingNorm word ≤ record.radius) ∧ (∀ input : List Bool, ¬ (language input = true) → ∃ record : BinarySyndromeDecodingInstance, encodeBinarySyndromeDecodingInstance record = map input ∧ 0 < record.blockLength ∧ 0 < record.radius ∧ (∃ word : Fin record.blockLength → ZMod 2, binarySyndromeProduct record word = binarySyndromeTarget record) ∧ ∀ word : Fin record.blockLength → ZMod 2, binarySyndromeProduct record word = binarySyndromeTarget record → binaryCodeGapFactor record.blockLength * (record.radius : ℝ) < (hammingNorm word : ℝ))) := by
  unfold IsNPHardPromise
  simp only [decide_eq_true_eq]
  constructor
  · intro h language hl
    obtain ⟨R⟩ := h language hl
    refine ⟨R.map, R.polynomial_time, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro input hin
      have := R.completeness input hin
      simpa only [binarySyndromeDecodingPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using this
    · intro input hin
      have := R.soundness input hin
      simpa only [binarySyndromeDecodingPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using this
  · intro h language hl
    obtain ⟨map, hp, hc, hs⟩ := h language hl
    exact ⟨{ map := map, polynomial_time := hp, completeness := fun input hin => by simpa only [binarySyndromeDecodingPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using hc input hin, soundness := fun input hin => by simpa only [binarySyndromeDecodingPromise, decide_eq_true_eq] using hs input hin }⟩
end GapCVP.Comparator
